author: reek
body: A child may not escape its parent's network scope by being born -- the twin of scope-runtime-spawn for the network authority.

author: reek
body: The process table copies the parent's capability MASK and its filesystem scope into a child at spawn; the network scope must travel beside them. If it did not, a program scoped to "ok.host" could spawn a child whose network-scope cell was zero, and a zero authority is an unscoped grant -- the child would inherit the right to reach the network and lose the limit on where, which is a capability amplification dressed as a fork.

author: reek
body: So the parent here is scoped to "ok.host" and does nothing itself. The child asks the gate about both hosts and reports both answers in one number: ten if the in-scope host is admitted, plus one if the out-of-scope host is admitted.

author: reek
body: Both net-scope-admits calls sit in argument position rather than a let bind, the same discipline scope-runtime-spawn keeps: nest, do not bind.
